CoSky 8.0 is a rewrite. A small server sits in front of Redis and gives applications configuration and service discovery, with access control on every call. Each application keeps a local view that a watch stream keeps current, so reading a Config or choosing an instance costs no round trip, and it keeps serving what it knows while the server is away. It replaces 6.x, whose applications talked to Redis directly. 6.x goes on, for bug fixes only, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

From here on, 8.x keeps what it has: within 8.x, the gRPC API, REST, the client's and the starter's API and properties, the server's properties, the documented metrics and the data in Redis only grow ([CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning)).

## Try it

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0 --dev
```

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes: a server in development mode, a Spring Boot application that reads a Config and registers, and another that finds it.

## What 8.0 brings

- **Configuration:** Spring Boot `spring.config.import` with live refresh; YAML, JSON, properties and text; revisions with rollback; zip import and export.
- **Service discovery:** Spring Cloud `DiscoveryClient`, `ServiceRegistry` and LoadBalancer; instances under a lease; metadata and weights; fixed instances.
- **Resilience:** local views keep serving through an outage, and a snapshot on disk survives a restart. A mass expiry, as after a network partition, is held back rather than obeyed. Several server replicas share one Redis, standalone, Sentinel or Cluster.
- **Security:** ServiceAccount tokens and OIDC on every call, applications included. Roles reach down to namespaces, kinds and name prefixes. TLS, and an audit log of every write.
- **Operations:** one image with the Dashboard, Kustomize manifests, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces.

The [documentation](https://cosky.ahoo.me/) covers each, with [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment), [Troubleshooting](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/troubleshooting) and [Backup and Restore](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/backup) for running it.

## `latest` is now 8.0

The image's `latest` tag now points to 8.0, on Docker Hub (`ahoowang/cosky:latest`), GHCR and Alibaba Cloud, and its `8.0` tag follows each 8.0 release. A 6.x deployment that pulls `latest` would start an 8.0 server, which reads none of the data of 6.x: name the version instead, such as `ahoowang/cosky:6.2.0`.

## Moving from 6.x

8.0 is a new system: applications on 6.x and on 8.0 cannot see each other, so they move together. [Moving from 6.x](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/upgrade-8) explains the cutover. `cosky-migrate`, attached to this release, imports the Configs and reports what to rebuild by hand. Applications move to Spring Boot 4.2 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.

## Upgrading from a release candidate

- **From rc.3:** a drop-in. Servers and applications can be upgraded in any order, and a rolling update can run both side by side. TODO(GA): what changed since rc.3, if anything did.
- **From rc.1 or rc.2:** a drop-in as well. Read the notes of each release since for what behaves differently.
- **From a beta:** as for rc.1, see [Upgrading from an 8.0 beta to rc.1](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/upgrading#from-an-8-0-beta-to-rc-1). The data in Redis carries over from beta.1 on.

## Requirements

- **Server:** JDK 25, which the image brings; Redis 7.0 or later, Redis 8 included, with `maxmemory-policy noeviction`; Kubernetes 1.27 or later for the manifests.
- **Applications:** JDK 21 or later, Spring Boot 4.2 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.

[Requirements](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/requirements) lists the rest.

## Known limits

TODO(GA): keep what the trial did not lift, and say what it verified, as the first item does.

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale, and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC is tested with Keycloak 26 only.
- **A Redis Cluster master that hangs with its connection open** pauses reaping in every namespace until the cluster marks it failed: `cluster-node-timeout`, 15 seconds by default. A node that is down does not.
- **On Sentinel,** while a master that hangs still holds the connection, the hints stop coming. Each replica then reads every namespace every second instead, and a write takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 35% of its CPU, as measured on rc.3. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Troubleshooting](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/troubleshooting#a-replica-cut-off-from-redis) shows how to notice.
- **A late Namespace creation that takes a write before it is undone** stays, without an object, and the server logs an error. That needs a write within the round trip between making the namespace and dropping it.
- **Removing every CoSky import at once** leaves their properties in place. A refresh that loaded no CoSky Config at all is not taken as one that ran the imports, so that nothing is dropped by mistake.

Thanks to everyone who ran the betas and the release candidates, and told us what broke. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you in 8.0.
